identity.title: Food Safety Plan — Ready-to-Eat Hummus and Bean Dips (Salem Plant)
identity.issuer: Willamette Valley Foods, Inc. (prepared by PCQI Dana Whitfield; approved by Plant Manager)

scan.summary: This is the company's written FSMA food safety plan for its Salem hummus and bean dip line, covering hazard analysis, preventive controls, monitoring, corrective actions, verification, a supply-chain program, records and training. It is the core document FDA and the Oregon Department of Agriculture would expect to see during an inspection to show the facility has identified its food safety hazards and put controls in place, but it is missing several elements 21 CFR Part 117 requires a complete plan to contain.
scan.freshness_note: Plan is effective May 12, 2025 and is just over a year old as of today. It does not state its own reanalysis schedule, but 21 CFR 117.170(a) requires reanalysis of the plan as a whole at least once every 3 years, which would put the next required reanalysis at or before May 12, 2028 (inferred — this date is not written in the document itself).

gaps.title: No written recall plan
gaps.description: The plan has no recall plan section. Sections 1 through 10 cover facility description, process flow, hazard analysis, preventive controls, monitoring, corrective actions, verification, supply-chain program, records and training, but there is no procedure for notifying consignees, conducting effectiveness checks, or disposing of recalled product.
gaps.fix: Add a written recall plan naming a recall coordinator, notification steps for direct consignees, procedures for public notification if applicable, effectiveness check methods, and disposition of recalled product.
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 117.139(a)-(b), required as a plan element by 21 CFR 117.126(b)(4)

gaps.title: No stated reanalysis schedule
gaps.description: Section 7, Verification, describes record review, calibration, product testing and environmental trending, but does not state that the plan as a whole will be reanalyzed at least once every 3 years or upon significant change, new hazard information, or an unanticipated food safety problem.
gaps.fix: Add a sentence in the verification or a new section stating the PCQI will reanalyze the food safety plan at least every 3 years and whenever a significant change or new hazard information arises.
gaps.quote: Environmental monitoring results are trended quarterly.

gaps.title: Supply-chain program lacks verification-activity detail
gaps.description: Section 8 states tahini and dry beans come only from approved suppliers who provide a third-party audit certificate and a certificate of analysis per lot, but it does not describe the actual verification activities the company itself performs (audit type/frequency, onsite audits, sampling and testing, or review of supplier records) or how supplier approval is documented and re-approved over time.
gaps.fix: Expand the supply-chain section to name the specific verification activity used for each supplier-controlled hazard (e.g., annual onsite audit, or COA review frequency), how often it recurs, and how approval/disapproval decisions are documented.
gaps.quote: Tahini and dry beans are received only from approved suppliers who provide a current third-party audit certificate and a certificate of analysis for each lot.

gaps.title: Plan approval not shown as signed and dated
gaps.description: The cover page names the approver only by title, 'Plant Manager,' with no printed name, signature or approval date next to it. The rule requires the plan to be signed and dated by the owner, operator, or agent in charge of the facility, both at initial completion and upon each reanalysis.
gaps.fix: Add the Plant Manager's printed name, a handwritten or electronic signature, and the date of approval on the cover page or a signature page.

gaps.title: No documented validation of preventive controls
gaps.description: Section 4 lists critical limits (e.g., 212°F for 60 minutes; cooling curve; ATP and Listeria swab program; metal detector reject sizes) but there is no reference anywhere in the plan to scientific or technical support, a validation study, or a citation showing these limits are adequate to control the identified hazards.
gaps.fix: Add a validation section or attachment citing the scientific/technical basis (e.g., a thermal process authority letter, published time-temperature study, or in-house challenge study) for each critical limit, particularly the cook and cooling steps.
gaps.locator: Section 4 (Preventive controls), page 4 — not in the document
gaps.quote: Minimum 212°F for 60 minutes, measured with a calibrated probe thermometer

gaps.title: No training records named
gaps.description: Section 10 states employees receive food hygiene training at hire and annually and that the PCQI holds an FSPCA certificate, but no training log, record, or retention reference is named for this training, unlike the cook, cooling, sanitation, allergen and metal detection logs named elsewhere in the plan.
gaps.fix: Name the specific training record (e.g., a training log or roster) that will be kept for hire and annual training, and confirm it is retained with the other records described in Section 9.
gaps.quote: All production employees receive food hygiene training at hire and annually.

gaps.title: Hazard analysis does not address chemical hazards
gaps.description: The hazard analysis table in Section 3 covers allergen, physical and biological hazards at each step but does not identify or evaluate chemical hazards such as pesticide/drug residues, natural toxins (e.g., mycotoxins in beans), heavy metals, environmental contaminants, or sanitation-chemical residue, nor does it record a conclusion of 'none identified' for chemical hazards.
gaps.fix: Add a chemical hazard column or rows to the hazard analysis addressing ingredient-related and process-related chemical hazards (e.g., mycotoxins in beans, sanitizer residue on food-contact surfaces) and document the conclusion, even if the outcome is that no preventive control is needed.

deadlines.title: Probe thermometer calibration
deadlines.source_line: Probe thermometers are calibrated in ice water and boiling water weekly

deadlines.title: Metal detector manufacturer service
deadlines.source_line: the metal detector is serviced by the manufacturer annually

deadlines.title: Finished product Listeria monocytogenes testing
deadlines.source_line: Finished product is tested for Listeria monocytogenes monthly by an accredited laboratory

deadlines.title: Environmental monitoring trend review
deadlines.source_line: Environmental monitoring results are trended quarterly

deadlines.title: PCQI review of corrective actions
deadlines.source_line: All corrective actions are recorded on the corrective action log and reviewed by the PCQI within seven days

deadlines.title: PCQI review of monitoring records
deadlines.source_line: The PCQI reviews the cook, cooling, sanitation, allergen and metal detection records within seven working days of their creation

deadlines.title: Employee food hygiene training
deadlines.source_line: All production employees receive food hygiene training at hire and annually

facts.value: Sesame (from tahini), declared on all hummus items
facts.quote: Products are labeled with the allergen statement "Contains: sesame" for all hummus items.
facts.affects: Confirms the allergen the company must control for label accuracy and cross-contact prevention.

facts.quote: for retail sale in Oregon, Washington and Idaho
facts.affects: Sets the multi-state distribution footprint relevant to recall notification scope and interstate commerce coverage under FDA jurisdiction.
Establishes that the plan's preparer held a PCQI credential before the plan's effective date, supporting 117.155(c)/117.180 PCQI requirements.
Drives the Listeria monocytogenes growth hazard evaluation and refrigerated storage preventive control in Sections 3-4.
Relevant to facility size classification and training record scope; also affects whether the small business 3-year reanalysis transition timelines applied at rule implementation.

facts.value: At least two years from the date of the record
facts.quote: kept at the Salem plant for at least two years from the date of the record
facts.affects: Sets the retention period against which all named logs (cook, cooling, sanitation, allergen, metal detection, corrective action) must be checked for completeness.

expected_missing.title: Oregon food processor license or registration from the Oregon Department of Agriculture
expected_missing.why: A facility manufacturing packaged ready-to-eat food for retail sale in Oregon would typically hold a state food processing license separate from the federal food safety plan.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: FDA Food Facility Registration confirmation
expected_missing.why: Facilities manufacturing food for U.S. consumption must register with FDA under the Bioterrorism Act/FSMA, and this registration number is usually kept alongside the food safety plan.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: Sanitation SOPs / Master Sanitation Schedule
expected_missing.why: The plan references ATP swabs and washdowns as a sanitation preventive control but points to no underlying written sanitation procedures document, which similar plants keep as a companion document.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: Environmental monitoring program with a swab site map
expected_missing.why: Section 4 and 7 describe weekly Listeria swabbing of 10 sites in zones 1 and 2, but the specific site locations and rotation are usually documented in a separate EMP map or SOP.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: Copy of the PCQI's FSPCA certificate
expected_missing.why: The plan cites the PCQI's March 2024 FSPCA training but companies typically keep the certificate itself on file to evidence the credential referenced on the cover page.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

scan.confidence_notes: I am confident in what the document contains because all quotes above are taken directly from the ten numbered sections as written. I am confident the six previously flagged gaps (recall plan, reanalysis schedule, supply-chain verification detail, signed/dated approval, validation, training records) are still open because none of the missing elements appear anywhere in this plan. I am less certain about how the company would defend the chemical-hazard gap in practice — it is possible a broader hazard analysis exists outside this document, in which case this finding would be resolved by producing that record. I have not verified whether Oregon has any state-specific overlay on top of 21 CFR 117 beyond the Oregon Department of Agriculture's role as the state regulatory partner named in Section 9.

WILLAMETTE VALLEY FOODS, INC.
FOOD SAFETY PLAN
Ready-to-eat hummus and bean dips
Salem Plant, 1850 Fairgrounds Road NE, Salem, Oregon 97301
Effective date: May 12, 2025
Prepared by: Dana Whitfield, Quality Manager, Preventive Controls Qualified Individual
(PCQI certificate, FSPCA course, March 2024)
Approved by: Plant Manager
1. Facility and product description
Willamette Valley Foods produces refrigerated ready-to-eat hummus and bean dips in 8-ounce and 16-
ounce sealed plastic tubs for retail sale in Oregon, Washington and Idaho. The Salem plant operates one
shift, five days a week, with 28 production employees. Products are made from cooked chickpeas or black
beans, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, salt and spices, blended, filled, sealed, coded and held
refrigerated at or below 41°F. Shelf life is 45 days refrigerated. Products are labeled with the allergen
statement "Contains: sesame" for all hummus items.
2. Process flow
Receiving of dry beans, tahini and other ingredients → dry storage or refrigerated storage → soaking and
cooking of beans (kettle, 212°F, 60 minutes minimum) → cooling in the blast chiller → blending with
other ingredients → filling and sealing → date coding → metal detection → refrigerated storage →
shipping.

5. Monitoring
The kettle operator records the internal temperature and the time at the start and end of each cook batch
on the cook log. The blast chiller operator records the temperature at 2 hours and at 6 hours on the cooling
log. The sanitation lead records the ATP swab result before each start-up. The line lead runs the three
metal test pieces through the detector at start-up, every two hours, and at the end of the run, and records
the result. The quality technician reviews every label lot against the formulation sheet at receipt and signs
the label log.
6. Corrective actions
If a cook batch does not reach 212°F for 60 minutes, the batch is re-cooked to the critical limit or
discarded, and the cause is recorded. If cooling exceeds the time limits, the batch is discarded. If an ATP
swab fails, the surface is re-cleaned and re-swabbed before production starts. If a Listeria spp. swab is
positive, the site is cleaned and re-swabbed, adjacent sites are added, and product made on that line since
the last negative swab is held pending investigation. If the metal detector fails a test piece, all product
since the last passing test is re-run through the detector. If a label does not match the formulation, the lot
is quarantined and not used. All corrective actions are recorded on the corrective action log and reviewed
by the PCQI within seven days.
7. Verification
The PCQI reviews the cook, cooling, sanitation, allergen and metal detection records within seven
working days of their creation. Probe thermometers are calibrated in ice water and boiling water weekly,
and the metal detector is serviced by the manufacturer annually. Finished product is tested for Listeria
monocytogenes monthly by an accredited laboratory. Environmental monitoring results are trended
quarterly.
8. Supply-chain program
Tahini and dry beans are received only from approved suppliers who provide a current third-party audit
certificate and a certificate of analysis for each lot. The approved supplier list is maintained by the quality
manager.
9. Records
All records named in this plan are kept at the Salem plant for at least two years from the date of the record
and are available to FDA and the Oregon Department of Agriculture on request. Records are reviewed and
signed by the PCQI as described in section 7.
10. Training
All production employees receive food hygiene training at hire and annually. The PCQI holds a current
FSPCA certificate. Sanitation and line leads are trained on the monitoring procedures in this plan.
